module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Nat.Even
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.TypeTags.Finite
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.TypeTags.Hom
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Equiv.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.GeomSum
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Parity
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Units
public import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Basic
public import MathlibExt.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Rotate
public import Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.Basic
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Cons

/-!
# Signed cyclic rotations of tensor powers

Reindexing a tensor power moves its last factor to the first. Over a commutative
ring, multiplying this rotation by the canonical unit `(-1)^n` gives a linear
automorphism of period `n + 1`. Its integer powers descend through `ZMod.lift`
to an actual cyclic representation. The associated norm satisfies both finite
geometric-sum identities and is natural under arbitrary linear maps.

The constructions allow the zero ring and arbitrary modules. No inverse of the
number of factors is used.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u v w

namespace TensorPower

/-- The index rotation has period equal to the number of tensor factors. -/
theorem rotationIndex_period (n : ℕ) : finRotate (n + 1) ^ (n + 1) = 1 :=
  finRotate_pow_succ n

section Unsigned

variable (k : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommSemiring k] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module k M]

/-- Move the final factor of a tensor power to its first position. -/
def rotation (n : ℕ) : TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M :=
  PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (finRotate (n + 1))

/-- The native reindexing formula fixes the last-to-first direction of rotation. -/
@[simp]
theorem rotation_tprod (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    rotation k M n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1)).symm i)) :=
  PiTensorProduct.reindex_tprod _ _

/-- Powers of rotation are the corresponding powers of the index permutation. -/
theorem rotation_pow (n j : ℕ) :
    rotation k M n ^ j =
      PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (finRotate (n + 1) ^ j) := by
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    change LinearEquiv.refl k _ =
      PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (Equiv.refl _)
    exact PiTensorProduct.reindex_refl.symm
  | succ j ih =>
    calc
      rotation k M n ^ (j + 1) = (rotation k M n ^ j).trans (rotation k M n) := by
        rw [pow_succ', LinearEquiv.mul_eq_trans]
      _ = (PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M)
          (finRotate (n + 1) ^ j)).trans
          (PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (finRotate (n + 1))) := by
        rw [ih]
        rfl
      _ = PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M)
          ((finRotate (n + 1) ^ j).trans (finRotate (n + 1))) :=
        PiTensorProduct.reindex_trans _ _
      _ = PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M)
          (finRotate (n + 1) ^ (j + 1)) := by
        rw [pow_succ', Equiv.Perm.mul_def]

/-- The unsigned rotation returns to the original tensor after `n + 1` steps. -/
theorem rotation_period (n : ℕ) : rotation k M n ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
  rw [rotation_pow, rotationIndex_period]
  change PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (Equiv.refl _) =
    LinearEquiv.refl k _
  exact PiTensorProduct.reindex_refl

variable {k M} {N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module k N]

/-- Applying the same linear map to all factors commutes with rotation. -/
theorem rotation_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (rotation k M n x) =
      rotation k N n (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) x) :=
  PiTensorProduct.map_reindex (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (finRotate (n + 1)) x

end Unsigned

section Signed

variable (k : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M]

/-- Signed last-to-first rotation, using the canonical unit even for the zero ring. -/
def cyclicEquiv (n : ℕ) : TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M :=
  LinearEquiv.smulOfUnit ((-1 : kˣ) ^ n) * rotation k M n

/-- The signed automorphism is scalar multiplication by `(-1)^n` after rotation. -/
theorem cyclicEquiv_apply (n : ℕ) (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    cyclicEquiv k M n x = (-1 : k) ^ n • rotation k M n x := by
  change ((↑((-1 : kˣ) ^ n) : k) • rotation k M n x) = _
  simp only [Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val, Units.coe_neg_one]

/-- The signed pure-tensor formula. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicEquiv_tprod (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    cyclicEquiv k M n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      (-1 : k) ^ n •
        PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1)).symm i)) := by
  rw [cyclicEquiv_apply, rotation_tprod]

/-- The sign contributes an even exponent over one complete rotation. -/
theorem cyclicEquiv_period (n : ℕ) : cyclicEquiv k M n ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
  let s : TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M :=
    LinearEquiv.smulOfUnit ((-1 : kˣ) ^ n)
  let r := rotation k M n
  have hsr : Commute s r := by
    change s * r = r * s
    apply LinearEquiv.ext
    intro x
    change (↑((-1 : kˣ) ^ n) : k) • r x = r ((↑((-1 : kˣ) ^ n) : k) • x)
    exact (r.map_smul _ _).symm
  have hs : s ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
    have hsign : ((-1 : kˣ) ^ n) ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
      rw [← pow_mul]
      exact (Nat.even_mul_succ_self n).neg_one_pow
    change (DistribMulAction.toModuleAut k (TensorPower k (n + 1) M)
      ((-1 : kˣ) ^ n)) ^ (n + 1) = 1
    rw [← map_pow, hsign, map_one]
  change (s * r) ^ (n + 1) = 1
  rw [hsr.mul_pow, hs]
  have hOne : (1 : TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M) *
      r ^ (n + 1) = r ^ (n + 1) := _root_.one_mul (r ^ (n + 1))
  have hPeriod : r ^ (n + 1) =
      (1 : TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :=
    rotation_period k M n
  exact hOne.trans hPeriod

/-- Degree zero has no sign and only one tensor factor. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicEquiv_zero : cyclicEquiv k M 0 = 1 := by
  simpa only [Nat.zero_add, pow_one] using cyclicEquiv_period k M 0

/-- The signed rotation as an endomorphism, used in the norm and its identities. -/
def cyclicOperator (n : ℕ) : Module.End k (TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :=
  (cyclicEquiv k M n).toLinearMap

/-- The actual endomorphism has the signed last-to-first pure-tensor value. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicOperator_tprod (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    cyclicOperator k M n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      (-1 : k) ^ n •
        PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1)).symm i)) :=
  cyclicEquiv_tprod k M n a

/-- The endomorphism period is inherited from the actual linear automorphism. -/
theorem cyclicOperator_period (n : ℕ) : cyclicOperator k M n ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
  change (LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom
    (cyclicEquiv k M n)) ^ (n + 1) = 1
  rw [← map_pow, cyclicEquiv_period, map_one]

/-- The degree-zero endomorphism is the identity. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicOperator_zero : cyclicOperator k M 0 = 1 := by
  change (cyclicEquiv k M 0).toLinearMap = _
  rw [cyclicEquiv_zero]
  rfl

/-- Integer powers descend through the earned period to actual cyclic automorphisms. -/
def cyclicAutomorphism (n : ℕ) :
    Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1)) →*
      (TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :=
  AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeLeft <|
    ZMod.lift (n + 1) ⟨{
      toFun j := Additive.ofMul (cyclicEquiv k M n ^ j)
      map_zero' := by
        change cyclicEquiv k M n ^ (0 : ℤ) = 1
        exact zpow_zero _
      map_add' a b := by
        change cyclicEquiv k M n ^ (a + b) =
          cyclicEquiv k M n ^ a * cyclicEquiv k M n ^ b
        exact zpow_add _ _ _ }, by
      change cyclicEquiv k M n ^ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1
      simpa only [zpow_natCast] using cyclicEquiv_period k M n⟩

/-- The cyclic action retains the original integer-power formula. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicAutomorphism_intCast (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) :
    cyclicAutomorphism k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (j : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      cyclicEquiv k M n ^ j := by
  change Additive.toMul
    (ZMod.lift (n + 1)
      (A := Additive (TensorPower k (n + 1) M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M))
      _ (j : ZMod (n + 1))) = _
  rw [ZMod.lift_coe]
  rfl

/-- The residue class of one acts by the signed rotation. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicAutomorphism_generator (n : ℕ) :
    cyclicAutomorphism k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      cyclicEquiv k M n := by
  simpa only [Int.cast_one, zpow_one] using cyclicAutomorphism_intCast k M n 1

/-- The actual linear representation of the cyclic group on a tensor power. -/
def cyclicRepresentation (n : ℕ) :
    Representation k (Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1))) (TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :=
  LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom.comp (cyclicAutomorphism k M n)

/-- Nonnegative residue classes act by powers of the signed endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicRepresentation_natCast (n j : ℕ) :
    cyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (j : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      cyclicOperator k M n ^ j := by
  have h := cyclicAutomorphism_intCast k M n (j : ℤ)
  simp only [Int.cast_natCast, zpow_natCast] at h
  change LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom
    (cyclicAutomorphism k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (j : ZMod (n + 1)))) = _
  rw [h, map_pow]
  rfl

/-- The generator of the representation is the original signed endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem cyclicRepresentation_generator (n : ℕ) :
    cyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      cyclicOperator k M n := by
  simpa only [Nat.cast_one, pow_one] using cyclicRepresentation_natCast k M n 1

/-- The cyclic norm is the finite sum of powers of the actual signed operator. -/
def norm (n : ℕ) : Module.End k (TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), cyclicOperator k M n ^ j

/-- The geometric sum is the native finite-group norm of the actual representation. -/
theorem norm_eq_representation_norm (n : ℕ) :
    norm k M n = (cyclicRepresentation k M n).norm := by
  classical
  let e : Fin (n + 1) ≃ Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1)) :=
    (ZMod.finEquiv (n + 1)).toEquiv.trans Multiplicative.ofAdd
  have he (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
      e i = Multiplicative.ofAdd (i.val : ZMod (n + 1)) := by
    change Multiplicative.ofAdd ((ZMod.finEquiv (n + 1)) i) = _
    exact congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd
      (ZMod.natCast_zmod_val ((ZMod.finEquiv (n + 1)) i)).symm
  calc
    norm k M n = ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), cyclicOperator k M n ^ i.val :=
      (Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun j => cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) (n + 1)).symm
    _ = ∑ a : Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1)), cyclicRepresentation k M n a :=
      Fintype.sum_equiv e
        (fun i : Fin (n + 1) => cyclicOperator k M n ^ i.val)
        (cyclicRepresentation k M n) fun i => by rw [he, cyclicRepresentation_natCast]
    _ = (cyclicRepresentation k M n).norm := rfl

/-- Evaluating the norm gives the same finite sum of rotated values. -/
theorem norm_apply (n : ℕ) (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    norm k M n x = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) x := by
  change (LinearMap.applyₗ (R := k) x)
      (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) = _
  exact map_sum (LinearMap.applyₗ (R := k) x) _ _

/-- The norm on a one-factor tensor power is the identity. -/
@[simp]
theorem norm_zero : norm k M 0 = 1 := by
  simp [norm]

/-- The left telescoping identity follows from the earned cyclic period. -/
theorem one_sub_cyclicOperator_mul_norm (n : ℕ) :
    (1 - cyclicOperator k M n) * norm k M n = 0 := by
  simpa only [norm, cyclicOperator_period, sub_self] using
    mul_neg_geom_sum (cyclicOperator k M n) (n + 1)

/-- The right telescoping identity follows from the same finite geometric sum. -/
theorem norm_mul_one_sub_cyclicOperator (n : ℕ) :
    norm k M n * (1 - cyclicOperator k M n) = 0 := by
  simpa only [norm, cyclicOperator_period, sub_self] using
    geom_sum_mul_neg (cyclicOperator k M n) (n + 1)

variable {k M} {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module k N]

/-- Applying an arbitrary linear map to every factor intertwines the signed operators. -/
theorem cyclicOperator_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) :
    (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f)).comp (cyclicOperator k M n) =
      (cyclicOperator k N n).comp (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f)) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  change PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (cyclicEquiv k M n x) =
    cyclicEquiv k N n (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) x)
  rw [cyclicEquiv_apply, cyclicEquiv_apply, map_smul, rotation_natural]

/-- The native composition-power lemma propagates naturality to all nonnegative powers. -/
theorem cyclicOperator_pow_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n j : ℕ)
    (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) ((cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) x) =
      (cyclicOperator k N n ^ j) (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) x) := by
  have h := Module.End.commute_pow_left_of_commute (cyclicOperator_natural f n).symm j
  exact (DFunLike.congr_fun h x).symm

/-- Every cyclic group element is natural under the same arbitrary linear map. -/
theorem cyclicRepresentation_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ)
    (a : Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1))) (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (cyclicRepresentation k M n a x) =
      cyclicRepresentation k N n a (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) x) := by
  have ha : Multiplicative.ofAdd (a.toAdd.val : ZMod (n + 1)) = a :=
    congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd (ZMod.natCast_zmod_val a.toAdd)
  rw [← ha, cyclicRepresentation_natCast, cyclicRepresentation_natCast]
  exact cyclicOperator_pow_natural f n a.toAdd.val x

/-- The actual norm, including all its summands, is natural under linear maps. -/
theorem norm_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) (x : TensorPower k (n + 1) M) :
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (norm k M n x) =
      norm k N n (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) x) := by
  rw [norm_apply, norm_apply, map_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  exact cyclicOperator_pow_natural f n j x

variable (k M)

/-- Every signed power has its actual scalar and inverse-permutation pure-tensor value. -/
theorem cyclicOperator_pow_tprod (n j : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    (cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) • PiTensorProduct.tprod k
        (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1) ^ j).symm i)) := by
  induction j with
  | zero =>
      simp
      apply congrArg (PiTensorProduct.tprod k)
      funext i
      rfl
  | succ j ih =>
      have hs : (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) * (-1 : k) ^ n = (-1 : k) ^ (n * (j + 1)) := by
        rw [← pow_add, Nat.mul_succ]
      have he : finRotate (n + 1) ^ (j + 1) =
          (finRotate (n + 1) ^ j).trans (finRotate (n + 1)) := by
        rw [pow_succ', Equiv.Perm.mul_def]
      rw [pow_succ', Module.End.mul_eq_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply, ih,
        map_smul, cyclicOperator_tprod, smul_smul, hs]
      apply congrArg (fun x => (-1 : k) ^ (n * (j + 1)) • PiTensorProduct.tprod k x)
      funext i
      exact (congrArg (fun e : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1)) => a (e.symm i)) he).symm

/-- The inverse natural residue gives the forward-permutation tuple with the original sign. -/
theorem cyclicRepresentation_inverse_natCast_tprod (n j : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    cyclicRepresentation k M n
        (Multiplicative.ofAdd ((-(j : ℤ)) : ZMod (n + 1))) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) • PiTensorProduct.tprod k
        (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1) ^ j) i)) := by
  let T := TensorPower k (n + 1) M
  let E : T ≃ₗ[k] T := cyclicEquiv k M n
  let f : (T ≃ₗ[k] T) →* Module.End k T :=
    LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom
  have hmap : (E ^ j).toLinearMap = cyclicOperator k M n ^ j := map_pow f E j
  have hp (b : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
      (E ^ j) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k b) =
        (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) • PiTensorProduct.tprod k
          (fun i => b ((finRotate (n + 1) ^ j).symm i)) :=
    (congrArg (fun g : Module.End k T => g (PiTensorProduct.tprod k b)) hmap).trans
      (cyclicOperator_pow_tprod k M n j b)
  have hs : (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) * (-1 : k) ^ (n * j) = 1 := by
    rw [← mul_pow]
    simp
  have hAuto : cyclicAutomorphism k M n
      (Multiplicative.ofAdd (-(j : ZMod (n + 1)))) = E ^ (-(j : ℤ)) := by
    simpa only [Int.cast_neg, Int.cast_natCast] using
      cyclicAutomorphism_intCast k M n (-(j : ℤ))
  change cyclicAutomorphism k M n
      (Multiplicative.ofAdd (-(j : ZMod (n + 1)))) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) = _
  rw [hAuto]
  change (E ^ (-(j : ℤ))) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) = _
  apply (E ^ j).injective
  have hLeft : (E ^ j) ((E ^ (-(j : ℤ))) (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a)) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k a := by
    rw [zpow_neg, zpow_natCast]
    exact (E ^ j).apply_symm_apply _
  have hRight : (E ^ j)
      ((-1 : k) ^ (n * j) • PiTensorProduct.tprod k
        (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1) ^ j) i))) = PiTensorProduct.tprod k a := by
    rw [map_smul, hp, smul_smul, hs, one_smul]
    apply congrArg (PiTensorProduct.tprod k)
    funext i
    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
  exact hLeft.trans hRight.symm

end Signed

section ConsSigned

variable (k : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M]

/-- Signed rotation on the tensor product with a separate first factor. -/
def consCyclicOperator (n : ℕ) : Module.End k (M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :=
  (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm (TensorPower.cyclicOperator k M n)

/-- The actual cyclic representation in the separate first-factor tensor coordinates. -/
def consCyclicRepresentation (n : ℕ) :
    Representation k (Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1))) (M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :=
  (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm.toMonoidHom.comp
    (TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation k M n)

/-- The consNorm transported along the same computed tensor coordinates. -/
def consNorm (n : ℕ) : Module.End k (M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :=
  (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm (TensorPower.norm k M n)

/-- The cons coordinates intertwine the actual Book operator and the shared rotation. -/
theorem consCyclicOperator_coordinates (n : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consEquiv k M n (consCyclicOperator k M n x) =
      TensorPower.cyclicOperator k M n (consEquiv k M n x) := by
  change TensorPower.consEquiv k M n
    ((TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).symm
      (TensorPower.cyclicOperator k M n (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n x))) = _
  exact (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).apply_symm_apply _

/-- Every element of the cyclic group uses the same original tensor coordinates. -/
theorem consCyclicRepresentation_coordinates (n : ℕ)
    (a : Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1))) (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consEquiv k M n (consCyclicRepresentation k M n a x) =
      TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation k M n a (consEquiv k M n x) := by
  change TensorPower.consEquiv k M n
    ((TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).symm
      (TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation k M n a (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n x))) = _
  exact (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).apply_symm_apply _

/-- The consNorm retains its full tensor-power value. -/
theorem consNorm_coordinates (n : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consEquiv k M n (consNorm k M n x) =
      TensorPower.norm k M n (consEquiv k M n x) := by
  change TensorPower.consEquiv k M n
    ((TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).symm
      (TensorPower.norm k M n (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n x))) = _
  exact (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).apply_symm_apply _

/-- The printed last-to-first formula on the original pure tensor. -/
@[simp]
theorem consCyclicOperator_tmul (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    consCyclicOperator k M n (a 0 ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k (Fin.tail a)) =
      (-1 : k) ^ n •
        (a (Fin.last n) ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i : Fin n => a i.castSucc)) := by
  have hrot : (fun i => a ((finRotate (n + 1)).symm i)) =
      Fin.cons (a (Fin.last n)) (fun i : Fin n => a i.castSucc) := by
    funext i
    cases i using Fin.cases with
    | zero =>
      rw [Fin.cons_zero]
      apply congrArg a
      apply (finRotate (n + 1)).symm_apply_eq.mpr
      exact finRotate_last.symm
    | succ i =>
      rw [Fin.cons_succ]
      apply congrArg a
      apply (finRotate (n + 1)).symm_apply_eq.mpr
      exact (finRotate_of_lt i.isLt).symm
  apply (consEquiv k M n).injective
  rw [consCyclicOperator_coordinates, consEquiv_tmul, Fin.cons_self_tail,
    TensorPower.cyclicOperator_tprod, map_smul, consEquiv_tmul, hrot]

/-- The actual cons-level operator has period `n + 1`. -/
theorem consCyclicOperator_period (n : ℕ) : consCyclicOperator k M n ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
  have h := congrArg (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (TensorPower.cyclicOperator_period k M n)
  simpa only [map_pow, map_one, consCyclicOperator] using h

/-- The original degree-zero tensor level has identity cyclic operator. -/
@[simp]
theorem consCyclicOperator_zero : consCyclicOperator k M 0 = 1 := by
  simp only [consCyclicOperator, TensorPower.cyclicOperator_zero, map_one]

/-- Nonnegative residues act by the corresponding powers in cons coordinates. -/
@[simp]
theorem consCyclicRepresentation_natCast (n j : ℕ) :
    consCyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (j : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      consCyclicOperator k M n ^ j := by
  change (consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (cyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (j : ZMod (n + 1)))) = _
  rw [cyclicRepresentation_natCast, map_pow]
  rfl

/-- The generator acts by the cons-level signed operator, not a substitute map. -/
@[simp]
theorem consCyclicRepresentation_generator (n : ℕ) :
    consCyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod (n + 1))) =
      consCyclicOperator k M n := by
  change (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation k M n (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod (n + 1)))) = _
  rw [TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation_generator]
  rfl

/-- The Book consNorm is the geometric sum of powers of its actual operator. -/
theorem consNorm_eq_sum (n : ℕ) :
    consNorm k M n = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), consCyclicOperator k M n ^ j := by
  change (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), TensorPower.cyclicOperator k M n ^ j) = _
  rw [map_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  exact map_pow (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm _ j

/-- The geometric sum is also the native finite-group representation consNorm. -/
theorem consNorm_eq_representation_norm (n : ℕ) :
    consNorm k M n = (consCyclicRepresentation k M n).norm := by
  change (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm (TensorPower.norm k M n) =
    ∑ a : Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1)),
      (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm (TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation k M n a)
  rw [TensorPower.norm_eq_representation_norm, Representation.norm]
  exact map_sum (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm _ _

/-- The one-factor consNorm is the identity on the tensor product with a separate first factor. -/
@[simp]
theorem consNorm_zero : consNorm k M 0 = 1 := by
  simp only [consNorm, TensorPower.norm_zero, map_one]

/-- The first printed telescoping identity on the tensor product with a separate first factor. -/
theorem consOne_sub_cyclicOperator_mul_norm (n : ℕ) :
    (1 - consCyclicOperator k M n) * consNorm k M n = 0 := by
  have h := congrArg (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (TensorPower.one_sub_cyclicOperator_mul_norm k M n)
  simpa only [map_mul, map_sub, map_one, map_zero, consCyclicOperator, consNorm] using h

/-- The second printed telescoping identity on the tensor product with a separate first factor. -/
theorem consNorm_mul_one_sub_cyclicOperator (n : ℕ) :
    consNorm k M n * (1 - consCyclicOperator k M n) = 0 := by
  have h := congrArg (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n).conjRingEquiv.symm
    (TensorPower.norm_mul_one_sub_cyclicOperator k M n)
  simpa only [map_mul, map_sub, map_one, map_zero, consCyclicOperator, consNorm] using h

variable {k M} {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module k N]

/-- Apply a given linear map to the regular coefficient and every algebra factor. -/
def consLevelMap (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) :
    M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M →ₗ[k] N ⊗[k] TensorPower k n N :=
  TensorProduct.map f (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => f))

/-- Applying the identity to the coefficient and every tail factor is the actual identity. -/
@[simp]
theorem consLevelMap_id (n : ℕ) :
    consLevelMap (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[k] M) n = LinearMap.id := by
  simp only [consLevelMap, PiTensorProduct.map_id, TensorProduct.map_id]

/-- Native tensor map composition preserves the ordered coefficient and tail maps. -/
theorem consLevelMap_comp {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module k P]
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (g : N →ₗ[k] P) (n : ℕ) :
    (consLevelMap g n).comp (consLevelMap f n) = consLevelMap (g.comp f) n := by
  simp only [consLevelMap, ← TensorProduct.map_comp, ← PiTensorProduct.map_comp]

/-- The original tensor map is the native full tensor-power map in cons coordinates. -/
theorem consLevelMap_coordinates (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ)
    (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consEquiv k N n (consLevelMap f n x) =
      PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (consEquiv k M n x) := by
  change TensorPower.consEquiv k N n
      (TensorProduct.map f (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => f)) x) =
    PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f) (TensorPower.consEquiv k M n x)
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun (TensorPower.consEquiv_naturality f n) x

/-- The actual signed operators are natural under arbitrary linear maps. -/
theorem consCyclicOperator_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) :
    (consLevelMap f n).comp (consCyclicOperator k M n) =
      (consCyclicOperator k N n).comp (consLevelMap f n) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  apply (consEquiv k N n).injective
  change consEquiv k N n (consLevelMap f n (consCyclicOperator k M n x)) =
    consEquiv k N n (consCyclicOperator k N n (consLevelMap f n x))
  rw [consLevelMap_coordinates, consCyclicOperator_coordinates, consCyclicOperator_coordinates,
    consLevelMap_coordinates]
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun (TensorPower.cyclicOperator_natural f n)
    (consEquiv k M n x)

/-- Every cyclic group element is natural in the separate first-factor coordinates. -/
theorem consCyclicRepresentation_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ)
    (a : Multiplicative (ZMod (n + 1))) (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consLevelMap f n (consCyclicRepresentation k M n a x) =
      consCyclicRepresentation k N n a (consLevelMap f n x) := by
  apply (consEquiv k N n).injective
  rw [consLevelMap_coordinates, consCyclicRepresentation_coordinates,
    consCyclicRepresentation_coordinates, consLevelMap_coordinates]
  exact TensorPower.cyclicRepresentation_natural f n a (consEquiv k M n x)

/-- The full cons-level norm is natural under arbitrary linear maps. -/
theorem consNorm_natural (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (n : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n M) :
    consLevelMap f n (consNorm k M n x) = consNorm k N n (consLevelMap f n x) := by
  apply (consEquiv k N n).injective
  rw [consLevelMap_coordinates, consNorm_coordinates, consNorm_coordinates,
    consLevelMap_coordinates]
  exact TensorPower.norm_natural f n (consEquiv k M n x)

end ConsSigned

end TensorPower

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.PiTensorProduct.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic

/-!
# Insertion of one fixed tensor factor

This is the native multilinear universal-property construction, with no new
tensor carrier. The construction was used privately in the source-owned
matrix Morita operators; this neutral owner permits the actual conjugation
and general unit-frame consumers to reuse it. Only semiring/module structure
is needed.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace TensorPower

universe u v

variable (k : Type u) [CommSemiring k]
  {B : Type v} [AddCommMonoid B] [Module k B]

/-- Insert one fixed factor into the actual tensor power. -/
noncomputable def insert {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) (c : B) :
    TensorPower k n B →ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) B :=
  PiTensorProduct.lift
    (MultilinearMap.mk'
      (fun a : Fin n → B =>
        PiTensorProduct.tprod k (Fin.insertNth (α := fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => B) i c a))
      (by
        intro a j x y
        simp only [Fin.insertNth_update]
        exact (show MultilinearMap k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => B)
          (TensorPower k (n + 1) B) from PiTensorProduct.tprod k).map_update_add
            (Fin.insertNth (α := fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => B) i c a) (i.succAbove j) x y)
      (by
        intro a j r x
        simp only [Fin.insertNth_update]
        exact (show MultilinearMap k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => B)
          (TensorPower k (n + 1) B) from PiTensorProduct.tprod k).map_update_smul
            (Fin.insertNth (α := fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => B) i c a) (i.succAbove j) r x))

@[simp]
theorem insert_tprod {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) (c : B) (a : Fin n → B) :
    insert k i c (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (Fin.insertNth i c a) := by
  rw [insert, PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod]
  rfl

end TensorPower

module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Cons
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Quotient
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Isomorphisms

/-!
# Quotients of tensor powers and coefficient tensors

Quotienting every tensor factor by a ground submodule quotients the tensor
power by the span of pure tensors with a factor in that submodule. The same
statement retains an arbitrary coefficient module. All maps use the original
modules and linear maps; no algebra, unit or flatness hypothesis is needed.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct
open LinearMap

universe u v w z t

namespace TensorPower

variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k] {A : Type v} [AddCommGroup A] [Module k A]

/-- The original quotient map applied to every factor. -/
def quotientMap (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) :
    TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) :=
  PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => S.mkQ)

/-- Every pure tuple is sent to the tuple of its actual quotient classes. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientMap_tprod (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → A) :
    quotientMap S n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => S.mkQ (a i)) :=
  PiTensorProduct.map_tprod _ _

/-- The ground span of the pure tensors with a factor in the given submodule. -/
def quotientRelations (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) : Submodule k (TensorPower k n A) :=
  Submodule.span k {x | ∃ a : Fin n → A, (∃ i, a i ∈ S) ∧
    PiTensorProduct.tprod k a = x}

/-- There is no factor to quotient in degree zero. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientRelations_zero (S : Submodule k A) : quotientRelations S 0 = ⊥ := by
  apply le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
  apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
  rintro x ⟨a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
  exact Fin.elim0 i

/-- Quotient classes of pure tuples still span the target tensor power. -/
theorem quotientMap_surjective (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Surjective (quotientMap S n) := by
  intro y
  induction y using PiTensorProduct.induction_on with
  | smul_tprod c a =>
      choose b hb using fun i => Submodule.mkQ_surjective S (a i)
      refine ⟨c • PiTensorProduct.tprod k b, ?_⟩
      rw [map_smul, quotientMap_tprod]
      exact congrArg (fun x => c • PiTensorProduct.tprod k x) (funext hb)
  | add x y hx hy =>
      obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := hx
      obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hy
      exact ⟨x + y, map_add _ _ _⟩

/-- The stated tensor relations are killed by the actual quotient map. -/
theorem quotientRelations_le_ker (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) :
    quotientRelations S n ≤ LinearMap.ker (quotientMap S n) := by
  apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
  rintro x ⟨a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
  change quotientMap S n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) = 0
  rw [quotientMap_tprod]
  exact (PiTensorProduct.tprod k).map_coord_zero i
    ((Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero S).2 hi)

private theorem cons_tmul_mem_quotientRelations (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) (a : A)
    {y : TensorPower k n A} (hy : y ∈ quotientRelations S n) :
    consEquiv k A n (a ⊗ₜ[k] y) ∈ quotientRelations S (n + 1) := by
  let f : TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) A :=
    (consEquiv k A n).toLinearMap.comp (TensorProduct.mk k A (TensorPower k n A) a)
  have h : quotientRelations S n ≤ (quotientRelations S (n + 1)).comap f := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨b, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
    change consEquiv k A n (a ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k b) ∈ quotientRelations S (n + 1)
    rw [consEquiv_tmul]
    exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨Fin.cons a b, ⟨i.succ, by simpa using hi⟩, rfl⟩
  exact h hy

private theorem cons_tmul_mem_quotientRelations_of_first (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ)
    {a : A} (ha : a ∈ S) (y : TensorPower k n A) :
    consEquiv k A n (a ⊗ₜ[k] y) ∈ quotientRelations S (n + 1) := by
  let f : TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) A :=
    (consEquiv k A n).toLinearMap.comp (TensorProduct.mk k A (TensorPower k n A) a)
  have h : (⊤ : Submodule k (TensorPower k n A)) ≤
      (quotientRelations S (n + 1)).comap f := by
    rw [← PiTensorProduct.span_tprod_eq_top]
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨b, rfl⟩
    change consEquiv k A n (a ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k b) ∈ quotientRelations S (n + 1)
    rw [consEquiv_tmul]
    exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨Fin.cons a b, ⟨0, by simpa using ha⟩, rfl⟩
  exact h (show y ∈ (⊤ : Submodule k (TensorPower k n A)) from Submodule.mem_top)

/-- Right exactness gives precisely the advertised kernel, in every degree. -/
theorem quotientMap_ker (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.ker (quotientMap S n) = quotientRelations S n := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      rw [quotientRelations_zero]
      apply LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr
      have h : (zeroEquiv k (A ⧸ S)).toLinearMap.comp (quotientMap S 0) =
          (zeroEquiv k A).toLinearMap := by
        apply PiTensorProduct.ext
        apply MultilinearMap.ext
        intro a
        simp only [LinearMap.compMultilinearMap_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply,
          LinearEquiv.coe_coe, quotientMap_tprod, zeroEquiv,
          PiTensorProduct.isEmptyEquiv_apply_tprod]
      intro x y hxy
      apply (zeroEquiv k A).injective
      exact (DFunLike.congr_fun h x).symm.trans
        ((congrArg (zeroEquiv k (A ⧸ S)) hxy).trans (DFunLike.congr_fun h y))
  | succ n ih =>
      apply le_antisymm ?_ (quotientRelations_le_ker S (n + 1))
      have hker : LinearMap.ker (TensorProduct.map S.mkQ (quotientMap S n)) =
          LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker (quotientMap S n)).subtype.lTensor A) ⊔
            LinearMap.range (S.subtype.rTensor (TensorPower k n A)) :=
        TensorProduct.map_ker (hfg := LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ S)
          (hg := Submodule.mkQ_surjective S)
          (hfg' := (quotientMap S n).exact_subtype_ker_map)
          (hg' := quotientMap_surjective S n)
      have hleft : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker (quotientMap S n)).subtype.lTensor A) ≤
          (quotientRelations S (n + 1)).comap (consEquiv k A n).toLinearMap := by
        rw [LinearMap.lTensor_def, TensorProduct.range_map_eq_span_tmul]
        apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
        rintro x ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
        exact cons_tmul_mem_quotientRelations S n a (by rw [← ih]; exact b.property)
      have hright : LinearMap.range (S.subtype.rTensor (TensorPower k n A)) ≤
          (quotientRelations S (n + 1)).comap (consEquiv k A n).toLinearMap := by
        rw [LinearMap.rTensor_def, TensorProduct.range_map_eq_span_tmul]
        apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
        rintro x ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
        exact cons_tmul_mem_quotientRelations_of_first S n a.property b
      intro x hx
      change quotientMap S (n + 1) x = 0 at hx
      have hmem : (consEquiv k A n).symm x ∈
          LinearMap.ker (TensorProduct.map S.mkQ (quotientMap S n)) := by
        change TensorProduct.map S.mkQ (quotientMap S n) ((consEquiv k A n).symm x) = 0
        apply (consEquiv k (A ⧸ S) n).injective
        have h := DFunLike.congr_fun (consEquiv_naturality S.mkQ n)
          ((consEquiv k A n).symm x)
        change consEquiv k (A ⧸ S) n
            (TensorProduct.map S.mkQ (quotientMap S n) ((consEquiv k A n).symm x)) =
          quotientMap S (n + 1) (consEquiv k A n ((consEquiv k A n).symm x)) at h
        simpa only [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, hx, map_zero] using h
      rw [hker] at hmem
      have h := (sup_le hleft hright) hmem
      simpa only [Submodule.mem_comap, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
        LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using h

/-- The actual quotient of the tensor power by its factor relations. -/
def quotientEquiv (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) :
    (TensorPower k n A ⧸ quotientRelations S n) ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) :=
  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ (quotientMap_ker S n).symm).trans
    ((quotientMap S n).quotKerEquivOfSurjective (quotientMap_surjective S n))

/-- The quotient equivalence retains the classes of the actual factors. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientEquiv_mk_tprod (S : Submodule k A) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → A) :
    quotientEquiv S n (Submodule.Quotient.mk (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a)) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => S.mkQ (a i)) := by
  change (quotientMap S n).quotKerEquivOfSurjective (quotientMap_surjective S n)
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a)) = _
  rw [LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective_apply_mk, quotientMap_tprod]

variable (S : Submodule k A) (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M]

/-- The coefficient is retained, and only the tensor-power factors are quotiented. -/
def coefficientQuotientMap (n : ℕ) :
    M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) :=
  TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (quotientMap S n)

/-- Actual pure coefficient tensors map to their factorwise quotient classes. -/
@[simp]
theorem coefficientQuotientMap_tmul_tprod (n : ℕ) (m : M) (a : Fin n → A) :
    coefficientQuotientMap S M n (m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => S.mkQ (a i)) := by
  rw [coefficientQuotientMap, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearMap.id_apply, quotientMap_tprod]

/-- The coefficient version of the same ground tensor relations. -/
def coefficientQuotientRelations (n : ℕ) : Submodule k (M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A) :=
  Submodule.span k {x | ∃ (m : M) (a : Fin n → A), (∃ i, a i ∈ S) ∧
    m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a = x}

/-- The original quotient map remains surjective with arbitrary coefficients. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientMap_surjective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Surjective (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) :=
  TensorProduct.map_surjective (g := LinearMap.id) Function.surjective_id
    (quotientMap_surjective S n)

private theorem tmul_mem_coefficientQuotientRelations (n : ℕ) (m : M)
    {y : TensorPower k n A} (hy : y ∈ quotientRelations S n) :
    m ⊗ₜ[k] y ∈ coefficientQuotientRelations S M n := by
  have h : quotientRelations S n ≤
      (coefficientQuotientRelations S M n).comap (TensorProduct.mk k M _ m) := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
    exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
  exact h hy

/-- The kernel consists exactly of the stated degenerate coefficient tensors. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientMap_ker (n : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.ker (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) =
      coefficientQuotientRelations S M n := by
  have hker : LinearMap.ker (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) =
      LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker (quotientMap S n)).subtype.lTensor M) := by
    exact (_root_.lTensor_exact M (quotientMap S n).exact_subtype_ker_map
      (quotientMap_surjective S n)).linearMap_ker_eq
  apply le_antisymm
  · rw [hker, LinearMap.lTensor_def, TensorProduct.range_map_eq_span_tmul]
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨m, y, rfl⟩
    exact tmul_mem_coefficientQuotientRelations S M n m
      (by rw [← quotientMap_ker S n]; exact y.property)
  · apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨m, a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
    change coefficientQuotientMap S M n (m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) = 0
    rw [coefficientQuotientMap_tmul_tprod,
      (PiTensorProduct.tprod k).map_coord_zero i
        ((Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero S).2 hi), TensorProduct.tmul_zero]

/-- The quotient equivalence retains every original coefficient, in independent universes. -/
def coefficientQuotientEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    (M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A ⧸ coefficientQuotientRelations S M n) ≃ₗ[k]
      M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) :=
  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ (coefficientQuotientMap_ker S M n).symm).trans
    ((coefficientQuotientMap S M n).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
      (coefficientQuotientMap_surjective S M n))

/-- The actual pure coefficient representative of the quotient equivalence. -/
@[simp]
theorem coefficientQuotientEquiv_mk_tmul_tprod (n : ℕ) (m : M) (a : Fin n → A) :
    coefficientQuotientEquiv S M n
        (Submodule.Quotient.mk (m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a)) =
      m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k (fun i => S.mkQ (a i)) := by
  change (coefficientQuotientMap S M n).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
      (coefficientQuotientMap_surjective S M n)
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk (m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a)) = _
  rw [LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective_apply_mk, coefficientQuotientMap_tmul_tprod]

/-- The inverse takes an actual quotient-map value back to its original quotient class. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientEquiv_symm_apply_map (n : ℕ)
    (x : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A) :
    (coefficientQuotientEquiv S M n).symm (coefficientQuotientMap S M n x) =
      Submodule.Quotient.mk x := by
  apply (coefficientQuotientEquiv S M n).injective
  change _ = (coefficientQuotientMap S M n).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
    (coefficientQuotientMap_surjective S M n) (Submodule.Quotient.mk x)
  rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective_apply_mk]

variable {N : Type z} [AddCommGroup N] [Module k N]

/-- Killing the ground relation submodule is exactly killing its pure generators. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientRelations_le_ker_iff (n : ℕ)
    (f : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] N) :
    coefficientQuotientRelations S M n ≤ LinearMap.ker f ↔
      ∀ (m : M) (a : Fin n → A) (i : Fin n), a i ∈ S →
        f (m ⊗ₜ[k] PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h m a i hi
    exact h (Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩)
  · intro h
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨m, a, ⟨i, hi⟩, rfl⟩
    exact h m a i hi

/-- Universal descent through the actual factorwise quotient, for arbitrary ground maps. -/
def liftCoefficientQuotient (n : ℕ) (f : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] N)
    (h : coefficientQuotientRelations S M n ≤ LinearMap.ker f) :
    M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) →ₗ[k] N :=
  ((coefficientQuotientRelations S M n).liftQ f h).comp
    (coefficientQuotientEquiv S M n).symm.toLinearMap

/-- The universal map retains the original values before quotienting. -/
theorem liftCoefficientQuotient_comp (n : ℕ)
    (f : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n A →ₗ[k] N)
    (h : coefficientQuotientRelations S M n ≤ LinearMap.ker f) :
    (liftCoefficientQuotient S M n f h).comp (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) = f := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  change (coefficientQuotientRelations S M n).liftQ f h
    ((coefficientQuotientEquiv S M n).symm (coefficientQuotientMap S M n x)) = f x
  rw [coefficientQuotientEquiv_symm_apply_map, Submodule.liftQ_apply]

/-- The factorwise quotient is epic for actual linear maps. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientMap_cancel (n : ℕ)
    {f g : M ⊗[k] TensorPower k n (A ⧸ S) →ₗ[k] N}
    (h : f.comp (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) =
      g.comp (coefficientQuotientMap S M n)) : f = g := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := coefficientQuotientMap_surjective S M n x
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h x

variable {S M} {B : Type z} [AddCommGroup B] [Module k B]
  {T : Submodule k B} {M' : Type t} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module k M']

/-- Every ground-linear coefficient/factor map preserving the submodule gives the actual square. -/
theorem coefficientQuotientMap_naturality (g : M →ₗ[k] M') (f : A →ₗ[k] B)
    (h : S ≤ T.comap f) (n : ℕ) :
    (TensorProduct.map g (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => S.mapQ T f h))).comp
        (coefficientQuotientMap S M n) =
      (coefficientQuotientMap T M' n).comp
        (TensorProduct.map g (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => f))) := by
  have hmap (a : A) : S.mapQ T f h (S.mkQ a) = T.mkQ (f a) :=
    DFunLike.congr_fun (Submodule.mapQ_mkQ S T f (h := h)) a
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro m y
  induction y using PiTensorProduct.induction_on with
  | smul_tprod c a =>
      simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_smul, map_smul,
        coefficientQuotientMap_tmul_tprod, TensorProduct.map_tmul,
        PiTensorProduct.map_tprod, LinearMap.comp_apply, hmap]
  | add x y hx hy =>
      simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy, LinearMap.comp_apply]

end TensorPower

module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Cons
public import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Rotate

/-! # The last coordinate of the existing tensor power -/
@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorPower
universe u v

variable (k : Type u) [CommSemiring k] (M : Type v) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module k M]

/-- Place an actual last vector after the original tensor-power word. -/
def snocEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    TensorPower k n M ⊗[k] M ≃ₗ[k] TensorPower k (n + 1) M :=
  (TensorProduct.comm k (TensorPower k n M) M).trans
    ((consEquiv k M n).trans
      (PiTensorProduct.reindex k (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => M) (finRotate (n + 1)).symm))

/-- Cons followed by the native rotation preserves the original order before the last vector. -/
theorem snocEquiv_tmul (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M) (m : M) :
    snocEquiv k M n (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a ⊗ₜ[k] m) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (Fin.snoc a m) := by
  simp only [snocEquiv, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
    consEquiv_tmul, PiTensorProduct.reindex_tprod, Equiv.symm_symm]
  exact congrArg (PiTensorProduct.tprod k) (Fin.snoc_eq_cons_rotate a m).symm

/-- Splitting a pure word recovers its unchanged initial word and its actual last coordinate. -/
theorem snocEquiv_symm_tprod (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    (snocEquiv k M n).symm (PiTensorProduct.tprod k a) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod k (Fin.init a) ⊗ₜ[k] a (Fin.last n) := by
  apply (snocEquiv k M n).injective
  rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, snocEquiv_tmul, Fin.snoc_init_self]

end TensorPower

/-!
# Period of finite rotation

After `n+1` steps, rotation of `Fin (n+1)` is the identity. This index-only
fact is shared by tensor-power rotations and geometric cyclic simplices.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Fin.NatCast in
/-- Rotating through all `n+1` positions returns to the identity, including `Fin 1`. -/
theorem finRotate_pow_succ (n : ℕ) : finRotate (n + 1) ^ (n + 1) = 1 := by
  have h (j : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
      (finRotate (n + 1) ^ j) i = i + (j : Fin (n + 1)) := by
    induction j with
    | zero => simp
    | succ j ih =>
      simp only [pow_succ', Equiv.Perm.mul_apply, ih, finRotate_apply,
        Nat.cast_succ, add_assoc]
  apply Equiv.ext
  intro i
  rw [h]
  simp

module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Finset.NatAntidiagonal

/-!
# Projections in internally graded algebras

This file develops a reusable API for homogeneous projections in an internally
graded algebra `A = ⨁ i, 𝒜 i`. It provides general lemmas for homogeneous
projections governing membership, identity, vanishing, finite reconstruction, and
multiplicative behavior, intended for reuse in arbitrary graded-algebra settings
including tensor algebras and related graded constructions.

Main results:

* `GradedAlgebra.proj_mem`: the `i`-th projection lands in `𝒜 i`.
* `GradedAlgebra.proj_eq_self`: projection fixes elements already in its grade.
* `GradedAlgebra.proj_eq_zero_of_ne`: projection vanishes on a distinct grade.
* `GradedAlgebra.sum_support_proj_eq`: every element is the finite sum of its
  homogeneous projections over its decomposition support.
* `GradedAlgebra.exists_finset_sum_proj_eq`: existential finite reconstruction.
* `GradedAlgebra.proj_mul_eq_sum_antidiagonal`: for `ℕ`-graded algebras, the
  projection of a product is the antidiagonal sum of projected factors.

These are direct consequences of the `DirectSum.Decomposition` and
`GradedAlgebra` APIs.
-/

@[expose] public section

open DirectSum Finset

namespace GradedAlgebra

variable {ι : Type*} {R A : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] [AddMonoid ι] [CommSemiring R]
  [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] {𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A} [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]

/-- The homogeneous projection lands in its grade. -/
theorem proj_mem (i : ι) (x : A) : proj 𝒜 i x ∈ 𝒜 i := by
  rw [proj_apply (𝒜 := 𝒜)]
  exact (decompose 𝒜 x i).2

/-- Projection is the identity on elements already in that grade. -/
theorem proj_eq_self {i : ι} {x : A} (hx : x ∈ 𝒜 i) : proj 𝒜 i x = x := by
  rw [proj_apply (𝒜 := 𝒜)]
  exact decompose_of_mem_same 𝒜 hx

/-- Projection is zero on an element lying in a different homogeneous degree. -/
theorem proj_eq_zero_of_ne {i j : ι} {x : A} (hx : x ∈ 𝒜 i) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    proj 𝒜 j x = 0 := by
  rw [proj_apply (𝒜 := 𝒜)]
  exact decompose_of_mem_ne 𝒜 hx hij

open Classical in
/-- Every element is the finite sum of its homogeneous projections over its
decomposition support. -/
theorem sum_support_proj_eq (x : A) :
    (∑ i ∈ (decompose 𝒜 x).support, proj 𝒜 i x) = x := by
  classical
  have h_eq : ∀ i, proj 𝒜 i x = (decompose 𝒜 x i : A) := by
    intro i
    exact proj_apply (𝒜 := 𝒜) i x
  simp_rw [h_eq]
  exact sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x

open Classical in
/-- Every element equals a finite sum of its homogeneous projections. -/
theorem exists_finset_sum_proj_eq (x : A) :
    ∃ s : Finset ι, (∑ i ∈ s, proj 𝒜 i x) = x := by
  classical
  exact ⟨(decompose 𝒜 x).support, sum_support_proj_eq (𝒜 := 𝒜) x⟩

variable {𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A} [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]

/-- For an `ℕ`-graded algebra, projection of a product is the antidiagonal sum
of projected factors. -/
theorem proj_mul_eq_sum_antidiagonal (a b : A) (n : ℕ) :
    proj 𝒜 n (a * b) =
      ∑ ij ∈ antidiagonal n, proj 𝒜 ij.1 a * proj 𝒜 ij.2 b := by
  classical
  have h_proj_eq : ∀ (x : A) (k : ℕ), proj 𝒜 k x = (decompose 𝒜 x k : A) := by
    intro x k
    exact proj_apply (𝒜 := 𝒜) k x
  calc proj 𝒜 n (a * b)
      = (decompose 𝒜 (a * b) n : A) := by
        rw [h_proj_eq]
      _ = ((decompose 𝒜 a * decompose 𝒜 b) n : A) := by
        rw [decompose_mul]
      _ = ∑ ij ∈ antidiagonal n,
          (decompose 𝒜 a ij.1 : A) * (decompose 𝒜 b ij.2 : A) := by
        exact coe_mul_apply_eq_sum_antidiagonal (A := 𝒜) (R := A)
          (decompose 𝒜 a) (decompose 𝒜 b) n
      _ = ∑ ij ∈ antidiagonal n, proj 𝒜 ij.1 a * proj 𝒜 ij.2 b := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro ij _
        rw [h_proj_eq, h_proj_eq]

end GradedAlgebra

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Spectrum.Quasispectrum
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Ideal
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Operations
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Nilpotent.Basic

/-!
# Quasiregular two-sided ideals

A two-sided ideal is quasiregular when each of its elements is quasiregular,
equivalently when `1 + x` is a unit for every element `x` of the ideal.  Such
ideals are exactly the two-sided ideals contained in the Jacobson radical.

The terminology is deliberately distinct from Mathlib's commutative
`Ideal.IsRadical`, which concerns radical ideals in the prime-ideal sense.

## Main declarations

* `TwoSidedIdeal.IsQuasiregular`
* `TwoSidedIdeal.isQuasiregular_iff_exists_inverseCorrection`
* `TwoSidedIdeal.isQuasiregular_iff_le_jacobson_bot`
* `TwoSidedIdeal.IsQuasiregular.of_forall_isNilpotent`
* `TwoSidedIdeal.IsQuasiregular.matrix`
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u

namespace TwoSidedIdeal

variable {R : Type u} [Ring R]

/-- A two-sided ideal is quasiregular if each of its elements is
quasiregular. -/
def IsQuasiregular (I : TwoSidedIdeal R) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x : R⦄, x ∈ I → _root_.IsQuasiregular x

/-- Ideal-level quasiregularity is equivalent to invertibility of `1 + x`
for every member of the ideal. -/
theorem isQuasiregular_iff_forall_isUnit_one_add {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} :
    I.IsQuasiregular ↔ ∀ x : R, x ∈ I → IsUnit (1 + x) := by
  constructor
  · intro h x hx
    exact _root_.isQuasiregular_iff_isUnit.mp (h hx)
  · intro h x hx
    exact _root_.isQuasiregular_iff_isUnit.mpr (h x hx)

/-- A two-sided ideal is quasiregular exactly when every member has a
two-sided quasiregular inverse correction which again belongs to the ideal. -/
theorem isQuasiregular_iff_exists_inverseCorrection {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} :
    I.IsQuasiregular ↔
      ∀ x : R, x ∈ I → ∃ y : R, y ∈ I ∧
        (y + x + x * y = 0 ∧ x + y + y * x = 0) := by
  constructor
  · intro h x hx
    obtain ⟨y, hy₁, hy₂⟩ := _root_.isQuasiregular_iff.mp (h hx)
    have hy_eq : y = -(x + x * y) :=
      eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left (by simpa [add_assoc] using hy₁)
    have hyI : y ∈ I := by
      rw [hy_eq]
      exact I.neg_mem (I.add_mem hx (I.mul_mem_right x y hx))
    exact ⟨y, hyI, hy₁, hy₂⟩
  · intro h x hx
    obtain ⟨y, -, hy₁, hy₂⟩ := h x hx
    exact _root_.isQuasiregular_iff.mpr ⟨y, hy₁, hy₂⟩

/-- An element of the Jacobson radical has invertible `1 + x`.

The proof does not assume that the ambient multiplicative monoid is
Dedekind-finite: a left inverse is promoted to a two-sided inverse by showing
that its residual idempotent lies in the Jacobson radical and vanishes. -/
theorem isUnit_one_add_of_mem_jacobson_bot {x : R}
    (hx : x ∈ (jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R))) : IsUnit (1 + x) := by
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := (mem_jacobson_iff.mp hx) 1
  have hz₀ : z * 1 * x + z - 1 = 0 := (TwoSidedIdeal.mem_bot R).mp hz
  have hz₁ : z * x + z = 1 := sub_eq_zero.mp (by simpa using hz₀)
  have hleft : z * (1 + x) = 1 := by
    rw [mul_add, mul_one, add_comm]
    exact hz₁
  let e : R := 1 - (1 + x) * z
  have he_eq : e = z * x - x * z := by
    dsimp [e]
    rw [add_mul, one_mul]
    calc
      1 - (z + x * z) = 1 - z - x * z := by abel
      _ = (z * x + z) - z - x * z := by rw [hz₁]
      _ = z * x - x * z := by abel
  have he_mem : e ∈ jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R) := by
    rw [he_eq]
    exact TwoSidedIdeal.sub_mem (jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R))
      (mul_mem_left (jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R)) z x hx)
      (mul_mem_right (jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R)) x z hx)
  have haz_idem : ((1 + x) * z) * ((1 + x) * z) = (1 + x) * z := by
    calc
      ((1 + x) * z) * ((1 + x) * z) =
          (1 + x) * (z * (1 + x)) * z := by ac_rfl
      _ = (1 + x) * z := by rw [hleft, mul_one]
  have he_idem : e * e = e := by
    dsimp [e]
    calc
      (1 - (1 + x) * z) * (1 - (1 + x) * z) =
          1 - (1 + x) * z - (1 + x) * z +
            ((1 + x) * z) * ((1 + x) * z) := by noncomm_ring
      _ = 1 - (1 + x) * z - (1 + x) * z + (1 + x) * z := by
        rw [haz_idem]
      _ = 1 - (1 + x) * z := by abel
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := (mem_jacobson_iff.mp he_mem) (-1)
  have hw₀ : w * (-1) * e + w - 1 = 0 := (TwoSidedIdeal.mem_bot R).mp hw
  have hw₁ : w * (-1) * e + w = 1 := sub_eq_zero.mp hw₀
  have hwleft : w * (1 - e) = 1 := by
    calc
      w * (1 - e) = w * (-1) * e + w := by noncomm_ring
      _ = 1 := hw₁
  have he_zero : e = 0 := by
    calc
      e = 1 * e := (one_mul e).symm
      _ = (w * (1 - e)) * e := by rw [hwleft]
      _ = w * ((1 - e) * e) := by rw [mul_assoc]
      _ = 0 := by rw [sub_mul, one_mul, he_idem, sub_self, mul_zero]
  have he_zero' : 1 - (1 + x) * z = 0 := by
    simpa [e] using he_zero
  have hright : (1 + x) * z = 1 := (sub_eq_zero.mp he_zero').symm
  exact ⟨⟨1 + x, z, hright, hleft⟩, rfl⟩

/-- A two-sided ideal is quasiregular exactly when it is contained in the
Jacobson radical. -/
theorem isQuasiregular_iff_le_jacobson_bot {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} :
    I.IsQuasiregular ↔ I ≤ jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R) := by
  constructor
  · intro hI x hx
    rw [mem_jacobson_iff]
    intro y
    have hyx : y * x ∈ I := I.mul_mem_left y x hx
    have hu : IsUnit (1 + y * x) :=
      _root_.isQuasiregular_iff_isUnit.mp (hI hyx)
    refine ⟨↑hu.unit⁻¹, ?_⟩
    rw [mem_bot]
    calc
      (↑hu.unit⁻¹ : R) * y * x + ↑hu.unit⁻¹ - 1 =
          (↑hu.unit⁻¹ : R) * (1 + y * x) - 1 := by noncomm_ring
      _ = 0 := by rw [hu.val_inv_mul, sub_self]
  · intro hI x hx
    exact _root_.isQuasiregular_iff_isUnit.mpr
      (isUnit_one_add_of_mem_jacobson_bot (hI hx))

namespace IsQuasiregular

variable {I : TwoSidedIdeal R}

/-- An elementwise nil two-sided ideal is quasiregular. -/
theorem of_forall_isNilpotent
    (hI : ∀ x : R, x ∈ I → _root_.IsNilpotent x) : I.IsQuasiregular := by
  intro x hx
  exact _root_.isQuasiregular_iff_isUnit.mpr (hI x hx).isUnit_one_add

/-- A two-sided ideal whose underlying left ideal has a zero power is
quasiregular. -/
theorem of_pow_asIdeal_eq_bot (n : ℕ) (hI : I.asIdeal ^ n = ⊥) :
    I.IsQuasiregular := by
  apply of_forall_isNilpotent
  intro x hx
  refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
  have hxpow : x ^ n ∈ I.asIdeal ^ n := Ideal.pow_mem_pow hx n
  have : x ^ n ∈ (⊥ : Ideal R) := hI ▸ hxpow
  simpa using this

/-- Entrywise matrices over a quasiregular two-sided ideal again form a
quasiregular two-sided ideal. -/
theorem matrix (hI : I.IsQuasiregular) (n : Type*) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] :
    (I.matrix n).IsQuasiregular := by
  rw [isQuasiregular_iff_le_jacobson_bot] at hI ⊢
  calc
    I.matrix n ≤ (jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal R)).matrix n :=
      matrix_monotone n hI
    _ = jacobson (⊥ : TwoSidedIdeal (Matrix n n R)) :=
      matrix_jacobson_bot

end IsQuasiregular

end TwoSidedIdeal
